claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. Let me gather some information about your situation.

I understand you're asking about Child Benefit for Alex, who is 11 years old and lives with you in the UK.

I need to clarify one important detail: you mentioned that Alex has been in hospital or residential accommodation for 15 weeks (which is more than 12 weeks). According to the rules, after 12 weeks in hospital or residential accommodation, you can still receive Child Benefit if you regularly spend money on them.

**Could you please confirm whether you regularly spend money on Alex while they are in hospital/residential accommodation?** This would include things like buying clothes, toiletries, snacks, magazines, toys, or other items for them.

This information is crucial to determining your eligibility, as the rules state that for children in a UK hospital or residential accommodation for more than 12 weeks, you can continue to receive Child Benefit if you regularly spend money on them.

## Summary

I'm unable to make a definite determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

**Here's why:**

You meet the basic requirements - Alex is 11 years old, lives with you in the UK, and you're responsible for them. However, since Alex has been in hospital or residential accommodation for 15 weeks (which is more than the 12-week threshold), your continued eligibility depends on a key factor:

**Do you regularly spend money on Alex?**

According to the rules, after 12 weeks in hospital or residential accommodation, you can still receive Child Benefit if you regularly spend money on your child. This includes expenses like:
- Clothes
- Toiletries
- Snacks or treats
- Magazines or books
- Toys or entertainment
- Any other items for their comfort or wellbeing

**What you should do:**

Contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office directly to discuss your specific situation. They can assess whether your spending on Alex qualifies for the exception to the 12-week rule and provide you with a definitive answer about your eligibility.

You can contact them by phone or post - visit the government website at www.gov.uk for contact details.
